title: A Picnic Party in Wildest Africa
subtitle: Being a Sketch of a Winter’s Trip to Some of the Unknown Waters of the Upper Nile
short_title: A Picnic Party in Wildest Africa
summary: An account of an expedition of 1903–04 organised by W. N. McMillan, an American living in England, with his wife and a party of friends; written by one of them, C. W. L. Bulpett. From Khartoum they go by steamer up the White Nile and the Sobat to the Baro River and into the Abyssinian highlands, then march south across the Gelo and the Akobo to the Boma plateau and Mount Ungwala, mapping country that had not been surveyed, and return to the Baro. The book describes the camps, the boats, and the caravan, hunting for elephant and other game, a mutiny among the men, and the Nuer, Yambo, and Galla people and their chiefs. Long extracts from Mrs. McMillan’s journal are quoted. With photographs, drawings, and a map.
